corpus: Meridian Digital Lending: internal policy + US federal regulation and guidance
license_note: Federal documents are works of the US Government and in the public domain (17 U.S.C. 105). The internal policy is fictional and written for this course.

documents.title: Meridian Digital Lending: Unsecured Personal Lending Policy v3.2
Regulation B: Equal Credit Opportunity Act (12 CFR Part 1002), incl. Official Interpretations
documents.why_included: Adverse action notices: what a decline must tell the applicant (12 CFR 1002.9).

documents.title: Regulation Z §1026.43: Ability-to-Repay and Qualified Mortgage (current)
documents.why_included: How to verify income and debts and consider DTI. Mortgage rule, used here as an industry reference.

documents.title: Regulation Z §1026.43: Ability-to-Repay and Qualified Mortgage (as of 2020-06-01)
documents.why_included: Versioning trap: the older text still contains the 43% DTI limit for General QM loans, which the 2020 amendments replaced.

documents.title: Identity Theft Red Flags Rule (16 CFR Part 681)
documents.why_included: Identity-theft red flags; grounds the IDENTITY_MISMATCH escalation.

documents.title: Customer Identification Program for Banks (31 CFR 1020.220)
documents.why_included: Minimum identity information and verification procedures.

documents.title: CFPB Circular 2022-03: Adverse Action Notification Requirements in Connection With Credit Decisions Based on Complex Algorithms
documents.why_included: AI-specific guidance on explaining algorithmic declines. Withdrawn in 2025: retrieval must not present it as current.

documents.title: CFPB Circular 2023-03: Adverse Action Notification Requirements and the Proper Use of the CFPB's Sample Forms
documents.why_included: Specific vs generic decline reasons. Withdrawn in 2025.

documents.title: Interpretive Rules, Policy Statements, and Advisory Opinions; Withdrawal (90 FR, 2025-05-12)
